audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim at Blight & Pike 1976:56 section 8 in the text we hold layer. The deciding source is the sole dedicated phonology of the variety (IJAL, SIL fieldworkers), and both the newer specialist's open-access 2021 paper (downloaded now, PDF p.6: tonic syllable = usually first syllable of lexical roots) and the held Sierra Otomi grammar (Voigtlander & Echegoyen 1979:23-24: stress always on first syllable of the root, proclitics unstressed, alternating rhythm) agree with stem-initial primary stress plus alternating secondaries, i.e. the coded 10/100/1010/10100 pattern. No grammar, dissertation or instrumental study of Tenango Otomi stress exists to supersede it; the one unheld item (IJAL 2021, paywalled) is about grammatical tone and unlikely to change the classification. One note for the catalog, not a reclassify: all three sources locate primary stress on the first syllable of the stem/root

sources.quote: 'La lengua tiene tres tonemas distintos: alto (A), bajo (B) y ascendente (C), contrastivos (léxica y gramaticalmente) en sílaba tónica (usualmente la primera sílaba de las raíces léxicas); los tonos A y B también son contrastivos en algunos clíticos.'
